title: Constructible domain and finite normalization of system refinement inverses
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\ge1$. For each scheme $W$ below put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ on a fixed small representative of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\mathscr S_W$ for the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of these module sheaves, with componentwise morphisms commuting with the quotient transitions, and use its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathscr S_W)$ [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the simultaneous system functors $P_u=u^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ with $P_u\dashv R_u$, unit $\eta_u$, counit $\varepsilon_u$, and exact open extension $j_!$ of that node. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $i=1,2$, let $c_i=(j_i:X\hookrightarrow\overline X_i,p_i:\overline X_i\to Y)$ be compactifications of $f$, and let $u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ be a proper refinement, so $uj_1=j_2$ and $p_2u=p_1$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Define $\gamma_u:j_{2!}\to R_uj_{1!}$ to be the actual varying-ring proper/open mate for $(j_1,j_2,1_X,u)$: its inverse-image map is open base change followed by projection to the clopen component $X\to\overline X_1\times_{\overline X_2}X$, identity on this component and zero on its complement [lem-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-pasting]. Let $c_{p_2,u}:R_{p_1}\cong R_{p_2}R_u$ be the canonical direct-image compositor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition].

For every $K\in D(\mathscr S_X)$ with bounded constructible pro-etale cohomology at each level [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], $\gamma_{u,K}$ is invertible. For every $n\ge1$ there is $L_n\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$ and an isomorphism $\nu_X^*L_n\cong K_n$ [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]; evaluation of $\gamma_{u,K}$ is the constant-$A_n$ normalized proper/open mate $\gamma_Q$ of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] on $K_n$, and evaluation of $R_{p_2}(\gamma_{u,K}^{-1})c_{p_2,u}$ is exactly the comparison $\theta_u(K_n,L_n,\alpha_n)$ of [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism], for every such witness $\alpha_n$. No compatible choice of the $L_n$ is required.

Moreover let $M\in D(\mathscr S_X)$ and $N\in D(\mathscr S_Y)$ be normalized, meaning their transition-adjoints $\alpha_{m,n}:M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ (and those of $N$) are invertible [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Suppose their levels are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then $P_fN$ and $T=M\otimes^LP_fN$ are normalized with levels in $D^b_{ctf}$. If the level-$n$ Tor intervals of $M_n,N_n$ are $[a_n,b_n],[c_n,d_n]$, those of $(P_fN)_n,T_n$ can be chosen as $[c_n,d_n]$ and $[a_n+c_n,b_n+d_n]$. Under canonical scalar-extension comparisons the transition-adjoints are $f^{-1}\alpha^N_{m,n}$ and the strong monoidal scalar-extension comparison followed by $\alpha^M_{m,n}\otimes\alpha^{P_fN}_{m,n}$ [lem-pur-system-normalized-tensor-closure]. In particular the asserted inverse mates and finite normalizations apply to both $M$ and $T$. All bounds may depend on $n$; no normalization of $R_pj_!M$ and no faithfulness of derived evaluation on morphisms are assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition); agent strict-system domain and fixed-A_n normalization, with finite Tor preservation from blueprint lem-sf-tensor-ctf (i),(ii).

proof.text: For each positive level use the proved fixedDerivedOrigin argument of lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin. Compare ConstantScalarRestriction.restriction with the intrinsic proEtaleModuleRestriction by identity section maps; the sheafification-unit equation identifies their scalar actions. Intrinsic constructibility therefore becomes fixed-scalar constructibility. Finite support supplies lower and upper bounds, and exact scalar encoding carries cohomology and its vanishing to the fixed presentation. Apply bounded constructible essential surjectivity, then lift the bounded etale antecedent to D-plus using its lower bound. This is independent at each n.

Specialize VaryingRing.gamma_evaluation to the refinement square. Naturality of evalJ moves the canonical identity-edge factor through open evaluation, proving gamma_evaluation by functoriality. For invertibility, choose a bounded constructible origin at each level by step 1 and apply gamma_witness_evaluation from step 3. Its right-hand side consists entirely of isomorphisms. Cancel the invertible evaluation comparisons on the left, reflect isomorphisms through the exact fixed-scalar equivalence, and use joint detection by the semilinear level evaluations. No common bound, normalization, or faithfulness on system arrows is used.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open; refinement specialization, combined with the existing strict-system and site-normalization statements.

proof.text: Fix any witness $(L_n,\alpha_n)$ from step 1. The constant-$A_n$ normalization of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] identifies the evaluated mate, under the canonical site comparisons, with the finite etale proper/open map. Its refinement clause in [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] identifies that map with $\alpha_u$ on $L_n$. Here $L_n$ is bounded, hence bounded below, so the finite-etale-origin hypothesis holds. The schemes in the compactifications are finite type over $k$, and hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$). Therefore [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization] applies: the normalized finite map transported by the site comparisons is the named pro-etale map $\alpha_u(L_n)$ in [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism]. Naturality of the specified mate gives the explicit identity $e_n(\gamma_{u,K})=Ru_*j_{1!}(\alpha_n)\circ\alpha_u(L_n)\circ j_{2!}(\alpha_n)^{-1}$. This is exactly $\alpha_u(K_n,L_n,\alpha_n)$ of that definition. The same calculation starts with every witness, proving the asserted universal quantifier without choosing compatible witnesses.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open; refinement specialization, combined with the existing strict-system and site-normalization statements.

proof.text: Evaluation respects composition and the specified direct-image comparisons by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The canonical compositor is the one normalized by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. A functor sends an inverse to the inverse of its image: applying it to both inverse equations proves this directly. Consequently evaluation of $R_{p_2}(\gamma_{u,K}^{-1})\circ c_{p_2,u}$ is $Rp_{2*}(\alpha_u(K_n,L_n,\alpha_n)^{-1})\circ c_{p_2,u,n}$. Clause (b) of [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism] defines this very composite to be $\theta_u(K_n,L_n,\alpha_n)$. This proves equality of the finite maps themselves; it makes no inference about equality of system maps from their evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open; refinement specialization, combined with the existing strict-system and site-normalization statements.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-system-normalized-tensor-closure] first with $v=f$ and $P=N$. Since inverse image of the constant ring sheaf $(A_n)_Y$ is $(A_n)_X$, its hypothesis $C_n=v^{-1}B_n$ is satisfied. It gives normalized $P_fN$ with transition-adjoint $f^{-1}\alpha^N_{m,n}$. Apply the tensor clause of the same statement to $M$ and $P_fN$ over $X$. It gives normalized $T$ and exactly the strong monoidal scalar-extension comparison followed by $\alpha^M_{m,n}\otimes\alpha^{P_fN}_{m,n}$. These are the actual transition-adjoints, including their cocycles, even though $A_m\to A_n$ need not be flat.

source.place: Clause (7), compatibility with finite reduction; agent application of the existing normalized-system tensor and inverse-image theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], $(P_fN)_n=f^{-1}N_n$ and $T_n=M_n\otimes^L_{A_n}f^{-1}N_n$ under the canonical evaluation comparisons. At constant coefficients the specified inverse image is exact, so this is the finite-level derived pullback. Apply [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] to $N_n$ along the given separated finite-type $f$: the level remains bounded constructible with Tor interval $[c_n,d_n]$. Apply clause (ii) of [lem-sf-tensor-ctf] on $X$ to $M_n$ and this pullback: $T_n$ is bounded constructible with Tor interval $[a_n+c_n,b_n+d_n]$. Both results are applied separately for each $n$, so no common bound has been introduced.

source.place: Clause (ii), with lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude for the second tensor factor.

proof.text: The given levels of $M$ and the levels of $T$ just proved satisfy the hypothesis on $K$ in steps 1-4. Substitute $K=M$ and $K=T$ there. This supplies their inverse mates, witnesses and finite normalizations. All constructions take place in the ordinary system derived categories; neither this substitution nor any earlier step asserts normalization of $R_pj_!M$.

proof.text: For ordinaryDirect use the identity-on-sections fixedDirect comparison from def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport, conjugated by the identity-on-sections scalar encoding isomorphisms of step 1; sectionwise extensionality proves uniqueness. For ordinaryPull and ordinaryOpen take inverse adjunction mates through the encoding equivalences. They are invertible by the equivalence-edge mate lemma. The mate unit identity and cancellation prove the prescribed unit normalization, and injectivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence proves uniqueness. The scalarPull comparison remains the separately named postponed part already present in Lean.

proof.text: For restrictionDirect_existsUnique, assemble a natural transformation between the two constant-coefficient towers using coefficient naturality from def-sp-varying-ring-operations. Naturality at the arrow n <= m gives compatibility of the actual quotient maps with constant direct image. Adjunction transports this to the inverse-image coefficient square. Specialize the already proved identity-on-sections direct-image comparison of lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction and take its inverse. The required identity after forgetting scalars holds literally; faithfulness on sections proves uniqueness. For restrictionPull_existsUnique specialize the ordinary restriction-pullback isomorphism of the same node. Its direct-image comparison is the inverse of restrictionDirect by the common identity section formula and uniqueness. The mates unit identity then shows that the adjunction transpose of the pullback comparison is exactly the displayed scalar-restricted unit followed by restrictionDirect inverse. Injectivity of each Hom equivalence gives uniqueness.
